content.title: Mutations and Revalidation
content.hook: Imagine a user edits a project title and presses Save.
content.context:
There are at least three meaningful moments:

```text
user submits
     ↓
mutation starts
     ↓
server accepts or rejects
     ↓
UI reflects the result
```

The hard part is not the button. The hard part is keeping the UI and remote data aligned.
goals: Understand that changing remote data creates a synchronization problem: the UI must eventually reflect the result of the mutation.

content.question:
A user changes a project title from “Forge” to “Forge Academy”. The mutation succeeds.

What should happen next?

options.text: Only the button label should change forever.
The application should update or reload the relevant data so the displayed project reflects the saved result.
The route should always navigate away.
The application should ignore the result.

feedback.correct: A successful mutation changes data. The UI must reconcile with the new source of truth.
feedback.incorrect: A successful mutation changes data. The UI must reconcile with the new source of truth.

content.title: Optimistic vs confirmed UI
content.text:
Two common approaches are:

**Confirmed update:** wait for the successful result, then show the new server-backed value.

**Optimistic update:** show the expected new value immediately, while the real mutation is still in flight, and be prepared to recover if it fails.

Neither is automatically correct. The choice depends on how reversible the action is, how important immediate feedback is, and how failure should be handled.

content.title: Revalidation
content.text:
Some routing systems can automatically re-run route data after a successful mutation. React Router, for example, revalidates loader data after route actions complete.

The deeper concept is:

```text
mutation changes data
        ↓
revalidate related data
        ↓
render current truth
```

content.question:
Suppose the mutation fails.

What should a robust interface do?

options.text: Make the failure visible and keep the user’s recoverable input when appropriate.
Hide the error so the screen looks clean.

feedback.correct: Error handling is part of the interaction design. The user needs to know what happened and what they can do next.
feedback.incorrect: Error handling is part of the interaction design. The user needs to know what happened and what they can do next.

content.question:
A developer says, “Once the mutation request finishes, the job is done.”

What are they missing?

options.text: The application still needs to reconcile the visible UI with the mutation result.

feedback.correct: The remote data changed. The screen must reflect the result or explain the failure.
feedback.incorrect: The remote data changed. The screen must reflect the result or explain the failure.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** A mutation creates a synchronization problem between the user's interaction, remote data, and the current UI.
**Senior habit:** Every mutation should have an answer to three questions: what happens while it runs, what happens if it succeeds, and what happens if it fails?
